text: SAN MARINO SERVICE PRESERVATION MEASURE. To maintain existing funding which supports essential San Marino services including: police, fire, paramedic, emergency preparedness, repairing streets and sidewalks and other City infrastructure, providing youth and senior programs, and general government use; shall the City of San Marino measure be adopted extending the currently existing utility users tax at a rate of 6 percent, raising $2,620,000 annually, until ended by voters?
Mayor Chou; Vice Mayor Lo; Council Member Shepherd Romey; Council Member Chang; Council Member Chou

analysis.title: City Attorney's Impartial Analysis of Measure U

strong: CITY ATTORNEY’S IMPARTIAL ANALYSIS OF CITY OF SAN MARINO MEASURE U, AN UPDATE TO THE SAN MARINO UTILITY USER TAX TO EXTEND THE TERM OF THE TAX AND INCREASE THE TAX RATE FROM FIVE TO SIX PERCENT.

text: On June 10, 2026, the City Council unanimously voted to place Measure U on the ballot for consideration by the electorate at the consolidated California General Election on November 3, 2026. If approved by a majority of the City of San Marino (“City”) voters, Measure U would authorize the extension of the term of the Utility User Tax (“UUT”) and an increased tax rate from 5% to 6% (“Proposed Tax”). The Proposed Tax would be charged on Telecommunication Users, Video Users, Electricity Users, Gas Users, and Water Users (collectively referred to as “utility users”) under California Revenue and Taxation Code section 7284.2, and San Marino Municipal Code Chapter XXVI Article 3.

Under the current Municipal Code, utility users pay a UUT of 5% of the charge imposed by the utility service provider to the utility user, and the current UUT will automatically expire on March 31, 2027.

The Proposed Tax would increase the UUT rate from 5% to 6%. The Proposed Tax would eliminate the existing expiration date, and the Proposed Tax would remain in effect until ended by a majority of San Marino voters voting at a subsequent election.

The City estimates that the Proposed Tax would provide approximately $2,620,000 in annual revenue. Since the Proposed Tax is a general tax, revenue from the Proposed Tax would go into the City’s general fund to pay for any lawful City program, improvement, or service and could be used to fund the services identified in the ballot question.

By placing Measure U on the ballot, the City complies with California Constitution Article XIII C (Proposition 218) and California Government Code section 53723, both of which require the Proposed Tax to be approved by a majority of the voters voting in the election.
A “yes” vote on Measure U is a vote in favor of the extension of tax term and Proposed Tax rate of 6%.
A “no” vote on Measure U is a vote against the extension of tax term and Proposed Tax rate of 6% percent.
